chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not smell perfume while you are in the state of Ihram, nor anything in which there is saffron, and do not taste food in which there is saffron.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah, involving specific rituals and prohibitions.
key_terms.رَيْحَانٌ: Perfume or scent, generally referring to fragrant substances.
key_terms.زَعْفَرَانٌ: Saffron, a specific spice used here as an example of a substance with scent or color.

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on using saffron during Ihram in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies that saffron, being a distinctively scented substance, is prohibited for both olfactory and gustatory use during Ihram, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on avoiding anything that retains a unique fragrance. It highlights the juristic distinction between general scents and those with specific aromatic properties, ensuring pilgrims maintain ritual purity and focus. This ruling underscores the broader principle of abstaining from sensory distractions that might detract from the spiritual state of Ihram.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not smell the aromas and you are in Ihraam, nor anything wherein is saffron, nor eat a meal with saffron in it’.
en.sarwar: 12. Safwan has narrated from abu al-Mighra’ who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram washes his hand with saltwort. He (the Imam) said, ‘My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would wash his hands with white al-Hurud (saltwort).”’
